summary.whatChanges: Signed-cookie parsing now accepts cookies whose value is an empty string. The dot-separator index check in `parseSigned` was loosened from `< 1` to `< 0`, so a cookie like `name=.signature` is verified and returned as `''` instead of being skipped. Tests cover the empty-value case for both the parser and the cookie helper.
behaviorChanges: getSignedCookie / parseSigned now return '' for a validly signed empty-string cookie value, instead of omitting the key (previously undefined)
Signed cookies whose serialized form begins with '.' (empty value) are now signature-verified rather than silently skipped; an invalid signature on them yields false
Test helpers switched from truthiness checks to explicit `=== false` comparisons, so empty values are no longer reported as 'INVALID'
risks: Consumer code using truthiness (`cookie || fallback`) on signed cookie values can no longer distinguish an empty string from a missing/invalid cookie; only `=== false`/`undefined` checks are reliable
Callers that previously received `undefined` for empty signed cookies now get `''`, which may change downstream branching
Malformed cookie values starting with '.' now enter the signature-verification path instead of being skipped early
